{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo matches exactly; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are identical) and come from the same UKB portability framework paper, with the same training cohort/size (UKB; n=391,124), the same selected validation ancestry and N (European; n=19,864), and the same basic covariates. Per the PRS Model Evaluator guidance (skill_overview + publication_context), publication/journal/date are weak differentiators here and mainly indicate this is a portability/framework study; since both are from the same framework, study context does not separate them.

Performance evidence is also essentially tied: neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; both report nearly identical partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563), which is not a strong basis for separation when endpoints/covariates are already matched.

Thus the decision falls to structural signals (skill_overview): method family/model structure and variant coverage. PGS002034 (LDpred2; 32,552 variants) is preferred over PGS001826 (penalized regression sparse model; 45 variants) as the more plausible genome-wide polygenic model when all other fields are equal.

Heritability sanity-check: the local h2 lookup for the exact target string returned only unrelated vitamin traits with match_score=0 (no meaningful h2 record for this rare coagulation-factor deficiency), so h2 cannot calibrate the observed partial-r; this limits confidence but does not change the within-list choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS005271","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Grounding in prs_model_evaluator skill sections (skill_overview, performance_metrics, publication_context) and trait h2 lookup: All three candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo=Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same disease-focused multi-ancestry thyroid disease study (publication_context notes that such titles are supportive context but weak for ranking). None provides PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC is reported with covariates marked Unknown, so per performance_metrics guidance, small full-model AUROC differences are not a reliable cross-model discriminator when covariate contribution is unclear. In this fallback setting, structural signals and effect-size evidence are more informative: PGS005271 (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants) has the strongest per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) among the candidates, consistent with stronger standalone PRS discrimination than PGS005272 (OR≈1.42) and especially PGS005270 (OR≈1.04), while also using a modern genome-wide Bayesian method rather than a sparse P+T score (55 variants). Heritability sanity-check was performed via get_heritability_records('hashimoto's thyroiditis') and returned no matching local h2 records, so no h2-based ceiling/context can be applied; confidence remains moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002082","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview + trait_labels): the target is lupus erythematosus (umbrella). PGS002082 has an exact trait_efo match (lupus erythematosus) and phenotyping_reported explicitly covers “Lupus (localized and systemic)”, which is well-aligned with the umbrella target. Several other candidates are narrower or shifted endpoints per trait_labels warnings (e.g., pediatric-onset SLE, lupus nephritis, renal disease/onset), making them less faithful for generic lupus erythematosus risk.

Performance/covariate interpretability (performance-metrics principles): many candidates only report full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, and one high-AUROC candidate (PGS003960) explicitly includes a phenotype risk score covariate, a packaging/leakage concern that makes its AUROC less comparable to standalone PRS quality. PGS002082 instead reports a PRS-focused metric (partial correlation) under standard demographic/PC covariates, which is more interpretable as genetic-score contribution.

Structural strength: PGS002082 uses a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2) with dense variant coverage (361,553) and very large development sample size (n=391,124), supporting broader polygenic signal capture than small genome-wide-significant-only scores.

Heritability sanity-check (get_heritability_records): local EUR records for systemic lupus erythematosus show substantial SNP-heritability (h2≈0.64; liability h2≈0.21, LDSC), consistent with lupus having meaningful common-variant signal and supporting the plausibility of a genome-wide PRS approach like PGS002082."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002037","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches to the target via trait_efo = nicotine dependence, and their trait_reported/phenotyping_reported (“Tobacco use disorder”) is a close synonym, so endpoint fidelity is acceptable. Per prs_model_evaluator procedural guidance (read_skill_section: skill_overview) and metric-handling guidance (read_skill_section: performance_metrics), when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent and candidates are from the same study family with similar covariates and validation design, we should not over-weight small metric differences; instead, use the best available PRS-comparable metric plus structural signals like method family and variant coverage. PGS002037 (LDpred2) has higher partial correlation in European validation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557) and much broader variant coverage (847,691 vs 13,838), which is generally favorable within the same publication/training context. Publication context (read_skill_section: publication_context) indicates both are UK Biobank portability-framework scores; since there is no disease-focused alternative in the candidate list, selecting the stronger sibling within this framework is appropriate. Heritability was queried with get_heritability_records for both “nicotine dependence” and “tobacco use disorder,” but no matching EUR h2 records were returned, so h2 cannot be used to further contextualize the partial-r magnitude; confidence remains Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000082","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Grounding in prs_model_evaluator skill sections:
- skill_overview: weigh endpoint fidelity, performance evidence, transportability/validation breadth, method/structure, and covariate cleanliness; express uncertainty when metrics are not PRS-only.
- trait_labels: prioritize phenotyping_reported for endpoint fidelity; exact label match is only a marginal advantage over near-synonymous endpoints with much richer evidence.
- performance_metrics: full-model AUROC/C-index are not PRS-only; covariate-heavy models can inflate discrimination; when PGS-only metrics are absent across candidates, structural/study-design signals and effect sizes matter more than small AUROC gaps.

Endpoint fidelity to target “ovarian neoplasm”:
- Exact EFO matches exist (PGS000544–PGS000564; malignant neoplasm of ovary; phenotyping_reported malignant neoplasm of ovary), but these are portability/framework-style PRSweb scores with consistently weak reported discrimination (AUROC ~0.52–0.57; pseudo-R² mostly ~0.002–0.011) and small evaluation samples (~5,196).
- Many non-PRSweb candidates are either special-population (BRCA1/2 carriers) or subtype-specific (serous/high-grade serous), which is less appropriate for a broad ovarian neoplasm target.

Why PGS000082 is the best single pick:
- It is a near-synonymous malignant ovarian endpoint (ovarian cancer; incident ovarian cancer) and, per trait_labels guidance, this near-synonymous direct disease endpoint can outweigh an exact-label but weak-evidence framework score.
- It has the strongest overall evidence package among broadly applicable ovarian cancer scores here: very large European evaluation (n=211,958) and the best reported discrimination in that general-population cluster (AUROC ~0.656 / C-index ~0.655). Although covariates are extensive (age, family history, reproductive/hormonal factors, PCs, etc.) so the AUROC is not interpreted as PRS-only, the combination of scale + disease-focused multi-cohort context + comparatively stronger discrimination makes it the most defensible choice.

Heritability tool evidence:
- get_heritability_records("ovarian neoplasm") returned no EUR matches.
- A broader lookup for "ovarian cancer" returned only non-cancer ovarian conditions (ovarian cysts/PCOS) with low observed h2; these records are not directly applicable to malignant ovarian neoplasm, so h2 cannot be used to calibrate expected PRS R²/AUC here and does not change the selection (it mainly limits confidence in any h2-based interpretation).

Overall: choose PGS000082 as the best-supported, broadly applicable ovarian malignancy PRS in this fixed candidate set, with moderate confidence due to lack of PRS-only metrics and imperfect h2 matching for the exact target label."}
